subject.title: [Bug]: cron agentTurn returns before foreground Bash subprocess completes — long-running executors are killed mid-stream, leaving partial state and a placeholder digest

question: Should isolated cron claude-cli agentTurn runs block/drain while CLI-owned foreground Bash/tool work is still pending, or should OpenClaw fail/signal/document that pattern as unsupported?
rationale: The source confirms the cleanup and green-run risk, but the permanent behavior affects orphan prevention, process-tree cleanup, cron run-record schema, Telegram delivery semantics, and possibly new telemetry or config surfaces.

options.title: Bounded drain plus failure signal
options.body: Detect pending CLI-owned tool work at turn end, wait only within the cron timeout/cleanup ceiling, and record timeout or forced cleanup as a non-green cron result when it cannot drain.

options.title: Telemetry first
options.body: Keep cleanup behavior for now but add a run-record diagnostic and operator-visible warning whenever a cron run ends with pending CLI tool work or forced process-tree cleanup.

options.title: Document unsupported foreground waits
options.body: Declare long foreground Bash-in-agentTurn cron jobs unsupported and steer users to command cron, systemEvent, detached tasks, or explicit disk-handoff patterns.

recommendation.title: Bounded drain plus failure signal
recommendation.body: Detect pending CLI-owned tool work at turn end, wait only within the cron timeout/cleanup ceiling, and record timeout or forced cleanup as a non-green cron result when it cannot drain.

likelyOwner.reason: obviyus has the strongest recent Claude live-session history in the affected cleanup path and is already tied to the overlapping lifecycle surface.
